name: Swedish Empire (Charles XII)

areaKm2.note: world_1700 Sweden polygon = 917,490 km2 on the sphere (Sweden, Finland, Baltic provinces, German territories). Ingria was lost in 1703; low subtracts it.

population.note: HYDE via OWID: Sweden 1,368,171 (1700) and 1,422,676 (1710); Finland 400,119 (1700) and 437,513 (1710); plus Estonia and Livonia ~0.3-0.4M and the German provinces (Swedish Pomerania, Wismar, Bremen-Verden) ~0.3M. Ingria lost 1703. Plague 1710-11 not yet.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share: Sweden 4.0% (1700, de Vries-type). Stockholm ~55,000, Riga ~15,000. Mid 5%.

activePersonnel.note: Effective strength peaked at ~100,000 in 1707-08 (Great Northern War article after Silfverstolpe 1864 p. 151 and Glete 2010 p. 206), nominal 110,000-115,000 (Chandler, Kennedy). Counted: the allotted (indelta) regiments and enlisted (varvade) regiments in the field, in Finland, the Baltic provinces and Pomerania, and garrisons, plus the navy. Snapshot is before Poltava (28 June 1709).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: replacement (tremanning/femmanning) levies and reserve regiments raised in 1709-10 from the allotment districts; Frost (Northern Wars ch. 12, isbn:0-582-06429-5) describes repeated extra levies.

supportPersonnel.note: Navy ~10,000-12,000 (43 ships of the line at peak, Glete 2010 p. 429 via the Great Northern War article; ~300 men per ship of the line in commission), artillery ~2,000, train and staffs.

mobilizationRatio.note: Sweden-Finland lost ~200,000 soldiers 1700-21 from ~2M people (Great Northern War article, Hoglund and Sallnas); peak strength ~100,000 = ~4% under arms; extreme ceiling 8-10%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Infantry ~55-60% of the ~100,000 effective (indelta and varvade regiments, garrisons). Main army in Ukraine before Poltava: 24,392 regulars incl. ~13,000 cavalry (Battle of Poltava article, Krotov 2014).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical) to 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: flintlock and bayonet, pikes still in the front rank, gå-på cold-steel tactics

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: Carolean veterans of Narva and Holowczyn; replacement drafts weaker

count.note: Cavalry regiments (indelta rusthall cavalry) charging knee to knee with the sword.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: good horses from the rusthall system; arme blanche

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: veteran shock cavalry, the best in northern Europe

count.note: Dragoon regiments (counted as light cavalry, as in the France 1805 snapshot); Swedish dragoons fought mounted like cavalry.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: as cavalry

count.note: Educated guess: Charles XII had 34 guns with the main army at Poltava (Battle of Poltava article), left most of the train behind; field guns in Finland, Livonia and Pomerania add the rest.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: good guns but neglected by Charles XII

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional gunners, little used

count.note: Swedish navy at peak: 43 ships of the line (Glete 2010 p. 429, Great Northern War article); ~38 in 1709.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Karlskrona-built ships of the line, Baltic-sized

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: trained crews, but navy starved of funds

count.note: Educated guess: frigates, galleys and skerries craft (Swedish archipelago fleet small before 1714).

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: Charles XII and Rehnskiold tactically brilliant (Narva 1700, Holowczyn 1708) but the 1708-09 Russian campaign over-reached; Lewenhaupt's supply column destroyed at Lesnaya

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75-1.0. Evidence: allotment regiments recruited from home parishes, Lutheran discipline; Carolean regiments fought on when surrounded

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: a decade of victories, but the winter of 1708-09 cost thousands to frostbite

weapons.note: Anchor: 5.5 between 1600 (5) and 1805 (6). Evidence: flintlock muskets and socket bayonets, pikes retained

armor.note: Anchor: 5.3. Evidence: cuirass largely abandoned except some cavalry

ships.note: Anchor: 5.5. Evidence: 70-gun ships of the line at Karlskrona

fortification.note: Anchor: 5.5. Evidence: Dahlbergh's Vauban-type fortresses at Riga, Narva, Stralsund

logistics.note: Anchor: 5.2. Evidence: magazines in the Baltic provinces; the 1708-09 Ukraine campaign depended on a supply column that was lost

communications.note: Anchor: 5.1. Evidence: courier post; Charles XII out of reach of Stockholm for years

isr.note: Anchor: ISR uses the same years as the anchor table (1600 -> 5, 1805 -> 6). Evidence: cavalry screens, spies and merchant reports only; no aerial or signal intelligence

air.note: No aircraft or military balloons before 1783/1794.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (2011 int$): Sweden 1700 = 2,002, 1709 = 1,824; Finland 1700 = 1,331. Mid weights Finland and the Baltic provinces in.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: wartime contributions from Poland and Saxony (1702-07) funded much of the war; Sweden itself was taxed to exhaustion by 1709. Peacetime share low.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: iron (the largest European bar-iron exporter), copper, gun founding.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: grain imports from Livonia and the German provinces; poor harvests in 1709.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.009-0.011 (mid 0.0095): in a pre-transition age structure (Wrigley and Schofield type, life expectancy ~30-35) males reaching 18 each year are about 0.9-1.1% of total population. Males only.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: royal roads between Swedish towns and the Finland coastal road; sea lanes carried most traffic.

majorPorts.note: Stockholm, Karlskrona, Gothenburg, Riga, Reval, Turku, Stralsund, Wismar, Stade.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: Swedish merchant fleet grew under the 1724-type navigation protections later; c. 1700 small.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-54657-5) ch. 1: 17th-18th c. armies tied to magazines and bread ovens, operating ~5 marches (~100-150 km) beyond the nearest magazine or navigable river; requisition extends it in rich country.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses (rusthall system supplied cavalry remounts) and oxen.

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: deep strategic depth, forest and lakes, harsh winters, sea moat; Sweden proper was not invaded until the 1719 Russian galley raids.

notes: Snapshot = early 1709, before Poltava (28 June 1709) and Perevolochna. Population counts Sweden, Finland, Estonia, Livonia and the German provinces. Personnel convention: allotted (indelta) and enlisted regiments in the field and in garrisons plus the navy are active; extra replacement levies are trainedReserves. The ~100,000 effective peak (1707-08) is the anchor; after Perevolochna (~15,000 surrendered) the field army was gone, so a late-1709 snapshot would be far weaker.
